== Biography ==
Samuel Glasgow passed away on 29 July 1857 in Killycurragh, County Tyrone. His will, containing one codicil, was proven at Armagh. The will’s executors were Andrew Thomas Ferguson of Cookstown and John Creighton of Tamlaght, both in County Tyrone. Samuel was a farmer in Killycurragh, and his estate was valued at under £200.<ref>PRONI Will Calendars: "The Will with one Codicil of Samuel Glasgon late of Killycuragh in the County of Tyrone Farmer deceased who died 29 July 1857 at Killycuragh aforesaid was proved at Armagh by the oaths of Andrew Thomas Ferguson of Cookstown and John Creighton of Tamlaght (Cookstown) in the said County of Tyrone the Executors."</ref><ref>http://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/reels/cwa/005014882/005014882_00057.pdf</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Working father review, 20 October 2026 ===

Prefer the William named in PRONI T1959/3 as Samuel Glasgow-1698’s probable working father, at 66% confidence. The positive case combines the expressly named Samuel in the letter, the exact Killycurragh family-farm setting, and the later Samuel’s documented farmer/probate household there in 1857. It replaces an unnecessary blanket hold with a testable family placement. The identity is less secure than James’s: there is no traced lease succession or age for the letter’s Samuel, and the current birth estimate may represent a later generation.

The percentages assess each entire father-to-profile proposition, including identification of the named son with the later profile; they are subjective comparative judgments, not measured frequencies. The original letter and holding succession remain unverified. Samuel’s circa-1800 birth is an estimate, and a materially older Samuel or a later same-name descendant is possible. His wife Anne’s approximate 1801 birth and their children in the 1820s–1830s do not date Samuel himself. A nephew or later tenant could share the name and townland. Do not transfer a recorded relationship to a later adult merely from the letter’s parent clause. William’s birth, death and own parents remain unknown. Miss Cunningham is retained as William’s reported wife, without selecting her as either profile’s mother. No existing person is merged or redated, and no live WikiTree edit has been made.

Inspect PRONI T1959/3 and associated family papers; test William’s identity against existing candidates and trace the Killycurragh holding through leases, rentals and valuation revisions. Establish Samuel’s age independently. The 1836 index date is probate information, not James’s exact death date.<ref>PRONI T1959/3; [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published family-letter transcription], earlier reviewed account reused; original not newly inspected. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/record-william-glasgow-killycurragh-t1959.html Sourced William Glasgow draft and identity comparisons].</ref>


From Samuel Glasgow’s will, we know the following about his family:

* '''Son:''' [[Glasgow-1697|Silas Glasgow]].
* '''Married Daughter:''' Sarah Mahood.
* '''Wife:''' Nancy Glasgow.
* '''Unmarried daughters:''' [[Glasgow-1835|Mary Jane (Glasgow) Parke (1836-1898)]] and [[Glasgow-1717|Adelaide Glasgow]].

In his will, Samuel refers to his residence as "the family mansion."

== Additional Family Connections ==

An interesting [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/3d923d3323349 marriage record] from 1863 at Owenreagh indicates a James Glasgow (widower), son of Samuel Glasgow. This family had another connection to Sixtowns through [[Loughlin-342|Isabella (Loughlin) Glasgow (abt.1823-1894)]], who was the wife of Silas Glasgow.

According to the '''Londonderry Standard''' marriage notice, Silas was Samuel’s eldest son.

=== Newspaper Mentions ===

In a [https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0001144/18571113/028/0003 newspaper article] from 13 November 1857, after Samuel’s death, he is listed as "Mr. Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh, Cookstown," one of the highest cesspayers in the barony.

=== Other Research Notes ===

Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh should not be confused with [[Glasgow-2054|Samuel Glasgow (abt.1792-1865)]] from Gortin, Derryloran, who died on a different date.

There is a possibility that [[Glasgow-2526|Samuel Glasgow (abt.1831-1902)]] was also a son, though he was not mentioned in the will.


An extensive interview with '''Mr. Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh''' was published in April 1844.<ref>https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/EPPI-1246182</ref>

A possible identification concerns Samuel Glasgow, farmer examined at Moneymore. An 1845 tenant-right discussion quotes Samuel Glasgow, described as an intelligent farmer examined at Moneymore, advocating secure tenure and protection against rent charged on improvements. He described seeing reclamation on Sir Thomas Staples’s land in his neighbourhood.<ref>Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 March 1845, p. 1, Ulster tenant-right discussion; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050103241/ record]; Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 March 1845, p. 1, alternate archive image of tenant-right passage; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1380777866/ record].</ref> Moneymore is where he was examined, not an explicit home townland. The date of his examination, age and relatives are unstated. Cookstown farmers [[Glasgow-2054]] and [[Glasgow-1698]] are compatible; [[Glasgow-2908|Lisnagaver Glasgow]] is a weaker regional comparison, without a locality or occupation bridge. No connection to Lisnagaver is established. The identification remains uncertain.
